- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is flat or rising, aggressively lower forecast to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- If true outcome shows sharp spike followed by sharp drop, model tends to over-forecast the spike — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high.  
- If model consistently over-forecasts early in 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5 days), apply downward bias of 2–3% to offset mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 0.0–0.4), model tends to underestimate true volatility — increase forecast variance by 10–15% for next 7 days.  
- When true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 3 days, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day mean, not 30-day trend.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.4–0.6) and forecast is flat, model often underestimates volatility — add 1–2% upward bias to reflect hidden risk.
